- Payment terms on PO-4567 show NET-30. Can you confirm whether Hydra requires invoice-level matching to PO line items or total-amount matching only? Our invoices can include the PO number and line-item breakdown but we want to align on the matching rule to avoid payment hold-ups.
- Tax handling: because we will invoice from Redwood Europe Ops (DE VAT: DE123456789), would you prefer a reverse-charge invoice (VAT 0% with reverse-charge note) or a gross VAT invoice? If Hydra is the recipient in Germany and subject to VAT reverse charge, we can issue the correct format.
- Beneficiary name: our legal banking name for the EU account is Redwood Inference Europe GmbH — IBAN and SWIFT attached. For US payments, benef name is Redwood Inference, Inc.

Attachments: filled_vendor_form.pdf (we pre-populated contact and remit fields), Redwood-EU-bank-info.pdf, redwood_w9_tax_letter.pdf

If you can confirm the matching rule and VAT preference I will finalize the vendor record today and confirm the vendor code so you can issue the PO.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement answers below: 

- Matching rule: Hydra requires line-item matching for any PO above €10k. For pilot PO-4567 (estimated €22k) we will perform line-item 3-way match. Please ensure invoice lists the PO line numbers and unit/quantity details.
- VAT: Hydra prefers a reverse-charge invoice for B2B services where possible — please include the standard reverse-charge text and reference our VAT ID (DE987654321). We will not pay VAT on your invoice if the reverse charge is correctly applied.
- Bank beneficiary: the vendor record must match the bank beneficiary name exactly to avoid rejections. We will accept Redwood Inference Europe GmbH for SEPA payments.

I'll go ahead and provision a provisional vendor code once I have the filled PDF and the bank IBAN that matches the beneficiary. If you can attach the final filled form and the EU bank confirmation we will accept the PO in our system.

Regards,
Lena
